record.provider: Bunny.net Edge Storage (+ free origin→CDN transit)

free_tier.stated: Unlimited volume, pay-as-you-go. $0.01/GB/mo HDD per region (up to 9 regions), $0.02/GB/mo SSD per region (up to 15). 20 TiB single-region HDD = $200/mo. $1 monthly minimum.

egress.terms: The structurally important bit: origin→CDN transit is free ('Free traffic to Bunny CDN', 'Free API egress'). Only end-user CDN delivery is billed, at $0.01/GB EU/NA, $0.03/GB Asia-Oceania, $0.045/GB South America, $0.06/GB ME-Africa. Or a flat $0.005/GB on the 10-PoP Volume Network. So storage and delivery are one bill with no double charge, unlike B2/R2-style metres.

record.tooling: S3-compatible API and an HTTP API, FTP/FTPS, plus rclone bunny backend. Limits are per-server: 100 concurrent HTTP connections per IP, 500 RPS per zone, 1 Gbps per connection. Documentation recommends sharding across connections.
record.chaining: Can front external storage origins such as Hetzner Storage Box or Bunny Storage ($10/TB) with Bunny CDN edge distribution ($5 to $10 per TB delivered). Pull zones can point to any origin endpoint and handle external delivery.
record.limits_note: per-ip-shaping: 100 concurrent conns per IP per server; 500 RPS per storage zone; 8 MB POST body for zip/download requests; 1 Gbps per connection. Geo-replication multiplies the storage price linearly (2 regions = 2x).
record.reliability_note: PCI/99.99% SLA on storage; $1 minimum means idle cost is trivial. Card required at signup is the binding constraint, and is why the free CDNs above matter more than Bunny's own storage.

record.provider: hop.js CDN (cdn.hopjs.net) — Bunny.net's free OSS mirror of npm + cdnjs

free_tier.stated: No quota of its own. It is a permanent mirror: every file is copied into Bunny Storage SSD and served from there, so your ceiling is the npm cap. Probed single files of 32.2 MB, 54.0 MB and 64.5 MB. All served complete and byte-identical to the unpkg copy (sha256 match on the 53,974,528-byte .node and the 64,458,752-byte .exe). No per-file cap was hit at any size tried.

retention.stated: No quota of its own. It is a permanent mirror: every file is copied into Bunny Storage SSD and served from there, so your ceiling is the npm cap

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. It is a free public CDN; no account, no key, no billing surface at all. Origin->CDN transit is Bunny's own storage, so there is no origin bill either.

record.tooling: Plain HTTPS GET: https://cdn.hopjs.net/npm/<pkg>@<ver>/<path>. No auth. Drop-in for any HTTP client / rclone http remote / curl. NOTE the path form carries the version twice when the mirror rewrites you, and the un-versioned form 302s to a broken URL. Always pin <pkg>@<ver> explicitly.
record.chaining: This is the missing piece for the npm-as-storage chain: publish the blob to npm (email-only identity), then serve it from hop.js instead of jsDelivr and the 50 MB jsDelivr file cap stops applying. Publish a 64 MB shard per npm version, chain thousands of versions, serve all of them free with no bandwidth ceiling. Because the mirror is permanent and Bunny-hosted, an npm unpublish does not remove the served copy in the short term.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: ~64 MB proven, likely bounded by npm's own ~100 MB tarball publish limit rather than by hop.js. cache-write-gated: only packages already in the npm/cdnjs index are mirrored. You cannot upload to hop.js directly, you publish upstream. /gh/ (GitHub) paths are not supported (404).
record.reliability_note: Young third-party service (Bunny-backed, 119 PoPs, logging disabled by design). Single point of failure with no SLA; Sustained single-stream measured 11.3 MB/s vs jsDelivr's 6.4 MB/s on the same 32 MB object.
